IncidentBot: :rotating_light: ALERT: elevated 5xx rate detected on gateway-prod (502/504 spike) — 3xx -> 20% -> 5xx. First observed 2025-01-12T14:57:56Z. PagerDuty: paging oncall Alex.
Alex: got the page, looking now. any obvious blast radius?
Lee: customer-facing dashboards show increased errors for the /v1/generate route. Top affected region: us-east-1.
Maya: I see a rise in connection timeouts to model-serving-tunnel-3; backend latency up from 30ms->700ms.
Alex: checking gateway logs... seeing 502 upstream: "connection reset by peer" from model-host-12.
Jordan: rolling deploy? any config pushes in last 30m?
Maya: no deploys in last 2h. Model-serving autoscaler logged frequent OOM kills around 14:52.
Alex: quick mitigation plan: 1) enable model-variant-fallback for traffic to use cpu-quantized variant 2) scale up model-serving pool + bring model-host-12 out of rotation 3) tighten per-customer rate limit for heavy customers temporarily. Doing (1) now.
Alex: //cmd
kubectl patch svc model-router -n prod -p '{"spec":{"trafficPolicy":{"fallbackVariant":"cpu-quant-1"}}}'
DeployBot: hotfix patch applied to model-router (rev r-2025-01-12-hotfix1)
Maya: fallback engaged, traffic now hitting cpu-quant-1, errors down from 21% -> 9% within 3m. latency still elevated ~200ms.
Lee: Customer-impact: 12 paying customers saw failures >= 2% for >5m. Support triage list created: cust_acme, cust_orbit, cust_spark.
Jordan: I'm scaling the serving pool by +4 nodes in us-east-1.
Alex: scaling command sent.
Maya: added node count, autoscaler catching up, starting to drain model-host-12 from LB.
IncidentBot: note: deploy r-2025-01-12-hotfix1 passed smoke tests.
Alex: monitoring SLOs and request traces. Setting alert suppression for related noisy 5xx alerts for 30m to avoid alert fatigue.
Jordan: temporary alert suppression set on alert_id:gateway_5xx_rate for 30m.
Lee: support notified customers in impacted list, message template used and sent.
Maya: after scaling, 5xx rate down to 2.2%, latency settled ~110ms. Looks healthy.
Alex: leaving a short post-incident checklist here: - hotfix applied (model-router fallback) - scale up completed - model-host-12 flagged for postmortem investigation - support notified - alert thresholds suppressed for 30m
Alex: handing off to Jordan for continued monitoring and post-incident actions. Jordan, take it from here, I'll be offline for next 45m. TL;DR: caused by model-host OOM leading to upstream resets; mitigated by fallback + scale.
Jordan: taking over. summary for handoff: current status: reduced 5xx ~2%, route stable. Immediate next steps for me: 1) run postmortem on model-host-12 memory usage 2) remove suppressions after 30m if metrics stable 3) open ticket to update runbook to include model OOM detection and automated fallback 4) tune alerts to use a rolling median over 5m instead of instantaneous spike.
Jordan: assigning action items: - @Maya investigate OOM causes and memory pressure on host-12 (owner: Maya) - @Alex to cut a quick postmortem doc when back online (owner: Alex) - @Lee to update customer status page and close support tickets (owner: Lee) - @Jordan to update alerts and runbook (owner: Jordan)
Maya: confirmed, I will collect heap dumps and recent prometheus metrics and post to the internal S3 folder.
Lee: will confirm support ticket updates and send final message to customers in 30m.
DeployBot: r-2025-01-12-hotfix1 rolled out to prod in 2 regions.
Jordan: plan to convene a 30min post-incident review tomorrow at 11:00 to go over root cause and long-term fixes.
Alex: thanks team. :white_check_mark: tagging IncidentBot for timeline capture.
IncidentBot: Timeline captured for thread 1754209876.
Jordan: leaving this thread open for notes; will update runbook PR link here once done. Action items recap: - Hotfix confirmed & rolled - Runbook update (alerts + automation) - Model-host investigation (OOM) - Postmortem doc + timeline - Customer comms closure
Lee: marking support tickets and drafting customer follow-ups. leaving status here once closed. :handshake:
